site.drive.change.backup.text: A full backup is easy. The mirror protects you from a drive failing; for a copy kept somewhere else, take one drive out and put a new one in: the device fills the new one, and the one you took out is your backup.

site.drive.change.hardware.text: You buy the hardware once. A Raspberry Pi 5 and two USB drives, mirrored so that each keeps a full copy. Your space is what one drive holds; when it fills up, you swap in bigger drives, one at a time, without stopping.

site.drive.change.more.text: More than a drive. The same device backs up every phone in the family in full resolution, keeps a photo library you can search, and runs your family's private social network.

site.drive.change.remote.text: Away from home, through the bridge. Your apps reach the device through our relay (free for two years, then €9.99 + VAT a year) or Tailscale Funnel, with no ports to open on your router, or through your own VPN.

site.drive.change.title.text: What changes when your files come home

site.drive.choose.dropbox.text: Dropbox if you want the most familiar sync, Linux included, and don't mind a monthly plan; passwords and expiry dates on links need Essentials or a business plan.

site.drive.choose.google.text: Google Drive if you live in Google's apps and edit documents together in the browser; it has no Linux app, and its space is shared with Gmail and Google Photos.

site.drive.choose.icloud.text: iCloud Drive if everyone in your family uses Apple devices: it's built in, with nothing to set up.

site.drive.choose.nextcloud.text: Nextcloud if you already run a server and want calendar, contacts and office apps too: it's free and open source, but installing it, reaching it from outside and backing it up are up to you.

site.drive.choose.otc.text: Off The Cloud if you want your family's files at home, with no monthly plan, on a device that's easy to set up and also backs up your photos and runs your private social network.

site.drive.choose.pcloud_mega.text: pCloud or MEGA if you'd rather avoid a monthly fee or want plenty of free space: pCloud sells lifetime plans, and MEGA gives 20 GB free.

site.drive.choose.proton.text: Proton Drive if you want storage from a privacy-focused cloud company, with open-source apps; there's no Linux app yet.

site.drive.choose.synology.text: A Synology NAS if you want a traditional NAS, with network drives for your computers and many apps, and don't mind choosing its drives and setting it up.

site.drive.compare.checked.text: Prices checked in October 2026. Cloud prices are per month unless the cell says otherwise. Off The Cloud and Synology are bought once, and they also use some electricity.

site.drive.compare.lead.text: Where your files live, what they cost and what each one does, as their own pages describe it.

site.drive.compare.title.text: Off The Cloud compared with Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive, Proton Drive, Synology and Nextcloud

site.drive.faq.fails.a.text: Nothing is lost: each of the two drives holds a full copy. The device carries on with the other one and tells you which to replace; put a new drive in its place and it copies everything back by itself.

site.drive.faq.fails.q.text: What happens if a drive fails?

site.drive.faq.network.a.text: Yes, through the sync app: the folders you add are ordinary folders on your computer, kept in sync with the device. What there isn't is a network drive (SMB) that opens the device's own storage directly, as a traditional NAS does.

site.drive.faq.network.q.text: Can I open my files from my computer's file manager?

site.drive.faq.private.a.text: Yes. Your files are stored encrypted on the device's drives, with a key only your password unlocks, and the password itself is never stored on it. Each person in the family has their own account and key, and nothing is used for ads or to train AI.

site.drive.faq.space.a.text: As much as one of your two drives holds, since each keeps a full copy. To grow it, swap the drives for bigger ones, one at a time: the device copies everything onto each new drive, then grows by itself, without stopping.

site.drive.faq.space.q.text: How much space do I get?

site.drive.hero.lead.text: Off The Cloud is free, open-source software that turns a Raspberry Pi 5 with two USB drives into your family's own file storage: a NAS that keeps folders on your computers in sync, backs up your phones and shares files with a link, with no storage plan to pay for every month. The same device is your family's private social network and photo library.

site.drive.hero.title.text: A home NAS instead of Google Drive or Dropbox

site.drive.keep.family.text: Space for everyone. Each person in the family gets their own account, with their files encrypted under their own password.

site.drive.keep.fast.text: Faster at home. At home the apps talk to the device over your own network, so big folders sync at Wi-Fi speed instead of your internet connection's upload speed.

site.drive.keep.links.text: Share links. Send files as a link that expires: whoever has it downloads them as a ZIP, with no account.

site.drive.keep.phone.text: Your files on your phone. Browse, open, upload and share them from the iPhone and Android apps, or from any browser in the web app.

site.drive.keep.sync.text: Folders in sync. The Mac, Windows and Linux apps keep the folders you choose in two-way sync with the device, or back them up one way, in the background.

site.drive.keep.title.text: What you keep from a cloud drive

site.drive.keep.versions.text: Nothing lost by mistake. Make a folder upload-only and nothing in it can be deleted, from any app; a file uploaded again under the same name keeps its earlier version.

site.drive.link.text: How it compares with Google Drive and Dropbox

site.drive.meta.description.text: Keep your family's files on a small NAS at home, in sync with your Mac, Windows and Linux computers and your phones, instead of Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive or Proton Drive.

site.drive.meta.title.text: Self-hosted Google Drive and Dropbox alternative | Off The Cloud

site.drive.move.desktop.text: From Dropbox, Proton Drive, pCloud and the like: if the service's app keeps a folder on your computer, make sure every file in it is downloaded, not online-only, then add that folder to the Mac, Windows or Linux app: every file goes to your device. Otherwise, download your files from the service's website first.

site.drive.move.google.text: From Google Drive: download everything with Google Takeout, which can turn Google Docs, Sheets and Slides into ordinary files, such as OpenDocument or PDF. Unzip it on a computer and add that folder to the Mac, Windows or Linux app.

site.drive.move.icloud.text: From iCloud Drive: on a Mac, copy the files into a folder of your own, outside iCloud Drive, and add that folder to the Mac app.
